'''Ivica Zubac''' (born 18 March 1997) is a Croatian professional [[basketball]] player who plays for [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Leks]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]].

==Career== 
He came through the youth ranks of [[KK Cibona|Cibona Zagreb]] and then played for KK Zrinjevac Zagreb in the second Croatian division during the 2013-14 season. He made the roster of Cibona Zagreb's men's team the following season, becoming a part of a group of prospects including [[Nik Slavica]] and [[Ante Žižić]] after the departure of [[Dario Šarić]]. He played in Croatia's top-tier A1 league and in the [[Adriatic League]] his first year and also saw action in the [[FIBA Europe Cup]] his second year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/fibaeuropecup/compID_BYg5Rb55Jw-G5I3MZ6JB01.season_2016.roundID_11866.teamID_1444.playerID_108416.html|title=Ivica Zubac {{!}} FIBA Europe Cup|website=www.fibaeurope.com|access-date=2016-04-01}}</ref> In February 2016, he left Cibona Zagreb because of the financial difficulties of the team, and signed with [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Leks]] of Serbia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.295.html:591198-Zubac-posvadjao-Cibonu-i-Cedevitu-a-potpisao-za-Mega-Leks|title=Zubac posvađao Cibonu i Cedevitu, a potpisao za Mega Leks|website=www.novosti.rs|access-date=2016-04-01}}</ref> By June 13, 2016, Zubac would be one of only 13 international underclassmen (as well as one of three Croatians) to enter their name in the [[2016 NBA Draft]], including three of his (ex)-teammates that previous season in [[Ante Žižić]], [[Timothé Luwawu]], and [[Rade Zagorac]].

== International career ==
Zubac represented the Croatian national teams at the U16 European Championships in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.season_2013.roundID_9441.playerID_108416.teamID_2168.html|title=Ivica Zubac {{!}} U16 European Championship Men (2013) {{!}} FIBA Europe|website=www.fibaeurope.com|access-date=2016-04-01}}</ref> He averaged 17.6 points and 7.9 rebounds a contest during the 2015 U19 World Championships in Greece,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/world/u19/2015/Ivica-ZUBAC|title=Ivica ZUBAC at the Players of the 2015 FIBA U19 World Championship - FIBA.com|website=FIBA.com|access-date=2016-04-01}}</ref> while receiving All-World Championships U19 Second Team honors by [[eurobasket.com]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/World-Championships-U19/basketball_2015_Men.asp|title=World Championships U19 Basketball, Teams, Scores, Stats, News, Standings - eurobasket.com|website=www.eurobasket.com|access-date=2016-04-01}}</ref> Zubac averaged double digits in scoring (15.8ppg) and rebounding (12.9rpg) to go along with 3.0 blocks per game at the U18 European Championships the same year,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://u18men.fibaeurope.com/en/compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2015.roundID_11484.teamID_2168.playerID_108416.html|title=Ivica Zubac {{!}} U18 Europe Championship Men - Division A|website=u18men.fibaeurope.com|access-date=2016-04-01}}</ref> while making the all-tournament second team (by [[eurobasket.com]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/European-Championships-U18/basketball_2015.asp|title=European Championships U18 Basketball, Teams, Scores, Stats, News, Standings - eurobasket.com|website=www.eurobasket.com|access-date=2016-04-01}}</ref>
